AC9 GATES — all green BY EXIT CODE on a clean tree, and the change is on Gerrit.

TREE afc99e250 (rebased onto current origin/main; ahead 1, behind 0). Working tree CLEAN — git status
--porcelain asserted EMPTY before the suite run, so the result is evidence about this commit rather than
about uncommitted scratch.
  make lint                            = 0
  make typecheck                       = 0
  python3 scripts/check_config_reads.py = 0     (config-read gate, ticket 6754)
  python3 scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check = 0   (env-drift; not stale)
  pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 6 --dist worksteal -q -p no:cacheprovider
      => 9374 passed, 41 skipped, 1 xfailed in 439.45s — EXIT 0
No gate was piped through grep or head; each exit code was captured directly.

PUSHED: Gerrit change 1289 ("1aa2: document local Bedrock gate opt-in"), commit carries the
rebar-ticket: 1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7 trailer, a Change-Id, and a DCO sign-off. Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and
Verified +1. The ticket will not close before Verified +1 — a passing completion verifier is not a
substitute for green CI.

WHY THE REBASE MATTERED: the branch was 16 commits BEHIND origin/main and 1 ahead. Gerrit CI runs the
TARGET branchs workflow, so a stale base invokes gate scripts the tree may not contain — the failure
mode that cost three stacks a full CI cycle earlier in this epic. Rebased before pushing, not after
diagnosing.

All nine acceptance criteria now have recorded evidence: AC1-AC3 from the Gate 1 run, AC4-AC5 from the
Gate 3 verify-completion run recorded above, AC6 the cachePoint TTL answer, AC7 the executed revert, AC8
the infra/ diff (0 files), AC9 the gates above.
